title: Tenant-aware memory signal fabricator for continuous batching and KV headroom
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: We currently rely on coarse heuristics (static watermarks + per-GPU headroom knobs) to budget GPU memory across weights, KV cache, and activations. This leads to either overly conservative headroom (wasted throughput) or reactive OOM spill events under mixed interactive and batch workloads. The goal of this ticket is to design and implement a tenant-aware Memory Signal Fabricator: a telemetry-driven service that synthesizes per-tenant and per-pool headroom budgets suitable for continuous batching and KV cache management while respecting weight residency constraints and activation peak profiles.

Proposal summary: Build a lightweight service that ingests fine-grained telemetry (per-request token counts, peak activation samples, KV cache occupancy by key namespace, eviction rates, GPU slab usage) and emits a set of memory signals every N seconds: recommended weight-residency budget, KV soft quota, activation transient allowance, and an emergency-spill threshold. Signals should be expressed as both absolute bytes and relative safety margins to ease integration with the runtime allocator. The fabricator will be tenant-aware (accounts for tenant priority and reservation tiers), GPU-aware (per-device headroom suggestions), and workload-aware (different signals for latency-critical vs throughput batch windows).

Design doc and artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Memory+Signal+Fabricator+Design
Initial prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2746
Telemetry schema PR (proto + docs): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412

Key constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: This ticket does not implement automatic enforcement of signals (that is a follow-up ticket). The runtime will consume signals via a stable API and we will iterate on enforcement once signals are validated.
- Must not increase serving latency tail by more than 2 ms at p99 due to signal enrichment paths.
- Signals must be resilient to sparse telemetry (graceful fallbacks to historical baselines).

Acceptance criteria:
- Fabricator service runs in staging and publishes a stable /v1/signals endpoint that returns per-tenant, per-GPU signals with versioned schema.
- Runtime can ingest signals via a polling path and expose an experimental flag to apply suggested soft KV quotas and activation allowances.
- Dashboard tiles in Console show the recommended vs applied headroom over time for at least two tenants in staging.
- PRs for the telemetry schema and prototype merged and smoke-tested under representative mixed workloads.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define minimal telemetry schema (per-request token histogram, peak activation sample, kv-occupancy stream) and submit telemetry PR.
2) Implement fabricator algorithm: rolling-window quantiles for activation peaks, tenant-priority weighting, and a ruleset for translating signals to absolute bytes and margin percentages.
3) Build service with two modes: assessment (read-only signals) and advisory (flags recommended hard/soft quotas).
4) Add runtime consumer hook behind a feature flag and an experimental admission controller that applies soft KV quotas (no hard eviction) and records divergence metrics.
5) Console dashboard work to visualize signals and divergence.

Tasks (short checklist):
- [ ] Finalize telemetry schema (owner: Rajat).
- [ ] Implement fabricator prototype algorithm (owner: Rajat).
- [ ] Add integration tests that replay telemetry traces and validate signal stability (owner: Syd Nguyen).
- [ ] Wire a read-only signals endpoint and document API (owner: Priya Sharma).
- [ ] Runtime feature-flag hook to consume signals (owner: Marcus Li).
- [ ] Console tiles and alert rules for large divergence (owner: Lina Ortega).
- [ ] Run 48h soak in staging against mixed interactive+batch workload and collect regression metrics (owner: SRE team).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Noisy telemetry could produce oscillatory signals leading to thrashing. Mitigation: Use hysteresis, damped moving averages, and quantile smoothing; add configuration for minimal update interval.
- Risk: Mis-calibrated signals cause premature KV evictions impacting latency. Mitigation: Start with advisory-only mode and conservative defaults; require opt-in rollout per tenant.
- Risk: Increased telemetry volume impacts cost. Mitigation: Use sampled telemetry and inline aggregation at host-side to reduce cardinality.

Notes on evaluation and rollout:
- Phase 1 (advisory): Fabricator publishes signals, runtime reads but does not enforce. Collect divergence and operator feedback for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (soft enforcement): Enable soft quotas for a pilot tenant (low-risk but representative). Monitor p50/p95/p99 latencies, OOM events, and cost/per-token.
- Phase 3 (wider rollout): After 1 month of stable results, enable for reserved pools with tenant opt-in.

Metrics to track:
- Signal stability: variance of suggested KV quota across 5-minute windows.
- Divergence: delta between suggested and applied (bytes and %).
- Incidents: number of OOM/spill events per 10k requests.
- Latency impact: p99 change vs baseline.
- Cost efficiency: tokens/sec per-GPU normalized by headroom.

Related tickets and references:

- ENG-462019 (gpu-pocket-budgeting-quota-model)
